note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: Nov 9: NZ election — Luxon's coalition holds a paper-thin 67-seat majority (Labour won the party vote 29.36% vs 29.21%); official result Nov 27 after special votes. Nov 9 NY close: kiwi +1.56% to $0.5616, strongest major, as the election overhang fades.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: Nov 9 NY close: Sep US wholesale inventories revised up to +0.7% (sales +2.8%, AI-linked electrical goods +2.5%); China CPI 0.7% miss vs PPI 5.7% beat (four-year high). Tuesday's US CPI is the next test.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: Nov 9 NY close: Brent $94.99 (-3.4%) and WTI ~$87.20 (-4.0%) ease the energy-inflation impulse into Tuesday's US CPI (fcst +0.3% m/m, core +0.2%, no y/y); gold ~$4,126 (+1.4%).
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Nov 9 NY close: Dec Fed hike ~82% (Reuters/CME FedWatch) into Tuesday's Oct CPI (7:30am CT); BoJ Dec hike ~80%, ECB Dec hike ~89% — the hike race is priced on both sides of the dollar.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). When nearly everyone has made the same bet, it can unwind fast: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: Oct 27 CFTC (released Oct 30): euro net short at a 3-yr low (non-commercial -143,894; contrarian +1 — squeeze side up); yen longs at the 98th percentile (contrarian -1); AUD/NZD shorts at 1st-percentile extremes (contrarian +1 each); GBP shorts at the 5th percentile (contrarian +1); CAD read is population-mixed, held neutral. Scores moved: GBP 3->4, JPY -1->-2, AUD 2->3, NZD 3->4. Next CFTC release Fri Nov 6, 2:30pm CT — the 4pm run picks it up. Nov 3 CFTC cut released Fri 2:30pm CT — percentile scoring vs the Oct 27 cut carries to the 2am run; board scores unchanged. Nov 3 CFTC (released Nov 6): EUR net short -157,791 (5th pct of 20y, 11-yr extreme) and JPY net long +102,321 (98th pct) still crowded; GBP's short unwound (+19,593 w/w to -59,821) out of the extreme — GBP positioning score 1 → 0. AUD -129,457 and NZD -60,015 still crowded short; CAD -41,775 after heavy covering (+24,649). Next CFTC cut (Nov 10 data) due later this week.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Nov 9 NY close: risk rebounds as Iran de-escalation hopes build — Nasdaq leads Wall St higher, VIX ~22.9 (-10.6%), DXY ~101.84 (-0.48%), NZD +1.56% and AUD +0.80% lead; the AI rout pauses.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Nov 9 NY close: Brent $94.99 (-3.4%), WTI ~$87.20 (-4.0%) as the Iran premium unwinds — the terms-of-trade tax keeps easing for importers; the crude tailwind is gone for CAD/AUD for now. Brent-WTI spread ~$7.8.
tot.title: Terms of trade
